newSounds: Four tones plus a neutral one: mā (1, high flat), má (2, rising), mǎ (3, falling-rising), mà (4, sharp falling), and a short neutral beat. Initials q = ch with a puff of air, x = sh with spread lips, c = ts, zh = a light j with the tongue curled back; ü has rounded lips like French u. r is light with the tongue curled, close to Telugu ర.
rhythm: Syllable-timed: one character = one syllable = one even beat, close to Telugu rhythm. There is no word stress; the tone on each syllable does the work that stress does in English.
registerFirst: nín is the polite 'you' and leads every phrase here; use it with strangers, elders and officials. nǐ is the casual form for friends and family.
trap: Tones are the whole job: mā, má, mǎ and mà are different words, so a wrong tone is a wrong word. This app teaches the tone patterns in writing; listening practice must come from an external source (a native speaker or audio course), never from reading pinyin alone. Common trap: third-tone sandhi — nǐ hǎo is said ní hǎo — plus the misleading initials q, x and c.
